# Mix Colour

Blends two colours or combines them with a chosen colour operation.

`lfs.mix_colour` · Utilities

## How to use

Connect colours to A and B; Factor 0.5 gives an equal mix.  
Start with Mix mode before trying Multiply or Add.  

## Inputs

| Name | Identifier | Type | Default | Range / choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | `A` | lfs.colour | [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] | step 0.01; accepts per-element values | First RGB colour, usually 0–1 per channel. The default is black. |
| B | `B` | lfs.colour | [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] | step 0.01; accepts per-element values | Second RGB colour, usually 0–1 per channel. The default is black. |
| Factor | `Factor` | lfs.float | 0.5 | min 0; max 1; step 0.01; accepts per-element values | Blend strength, 0–1. 0 keeps A, 1 uses the chosen operation fully; 0.5 gives a half-strength blend. |

## Outputs

| Name | Identifier | Type | Default | Range / choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Colour | `Colour` | lfs.colour | — | — | Resulting RGB colour. 0 is black and 1 is white per channel; some calculations can exceed this range. |

## Settings

| Name | Identifier | Type | Default | Range / choices | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mode | `mode` | enum | mix | mix; multiply; add; subtract | How you combine colours. Mix is the default; Add, Subtract and Multiply change the blend before Factor is applied. |
